title: Number of Adjacent Elements With the Same Color
summary: Given an array of zeros of length n, for each query, set the specified index to the given color and count the adjacent pairs with the same color, then return an array of counts for each query.
statement: Given an array of zeros of length n, for each query, set the specified index to the given color and count the adjacent pairs with the same color, then return an array of counts for each query.
constraints: Begin with n uncolored positions represented by zero.
Each query [index,color] replaces that position with a positive color.
After every query, return the number of adjacent pairs having the same nonzero color.
hints: Only pairs touching the updated index can change.
Before recoloring, subtract its matches with nonzero neighbors.
Assign the new color, add its new neighbor matches, and append the running total.
All untouched pairs preserve status, and the two local passes remove exactly the old contributions before adding exactly the new ones.
editorial: All untouched pairs preserve status, and the two local passes remove exactly the old contributions before adding exactly the new ones.

tests.explanation: The equal-adjacency counts after the five replacements are 0, 1, 1, 0, and 2.
A one-position array has no adjacent pair after either query.
